title: Depth of a finite module over a Noetherian local ring via Ext from the residue field
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], i.e. a Noetherian commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, let $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$, and let $M$ be a nonzero finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. For $i\ge0$ let $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(\kappa,M)$ be the $i$-th Ext group of [def-pc-ext] in the abelian category of $R$-modules. Then there is an integer $i\ge0$ with $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(\kappa,M)\neq0$, and the depth $\operatorname{depth}(M)=\operatorname{depth}_{\mathfrak m}(M)$ of [def-weil-pbc-depth] is finite and equals the smallest integer $i\ge0$ such that $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(\kappa,M)\neq0$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00LW (lemma-depth-ext, line 17863), proof lines 17870-17901; tag verified in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags: 00LW,algebra-lemma-depth-ext

proof.text: Put $d=\operatorname{depth}(M)$. Since $R$ is local, $\mathfrak m$ is its Jacobson radical. If $\mathfrak mM=M$, Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson] gives $M=0$, contrary to hypothesis. Thus $d$ is the supremum of lengths of $M$-regular sequences in $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-depth]. By [lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-support-dimension], $d\le\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)$; every chain in $\operatorname{Supp}(M)$ is a chain in $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$, so $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)\le\dim R$. The latter is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-finite-krull-dimension]. Hence $d$ is a finite nonnegative integer. We induct on $d$, keeping the statement for every nonzero finite module over a Noetherian local ring.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00LW (lemma-depth-ext), opening and induction; Definition Tag 00LI (definition-depth); Lemma Tag 00LK (lemma-bound-depth); Proposition Tag 00KQ (proposition-dimension)

proof.text:
An $R$-linear map $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m	o M$ is determined by the image $z$ of $1$; it is nonzero exactly when $z
eq0$, and it is well defined exactly when $\mathfrak m z=0$. For nonzero $z$, its annihilator is then precisely $\mathfrak m$ because $\mathfrak m$ is maximal. By [lem-weil-pbc-ext-zero-hom], $\operatorname{Ext}^0_R(\kappa,M)
eq0$ exactly when $\mathfrak m$ is an associated prime of $M$. By [lem-weil-pbc-nonzerodivisor-if-maximal-not-associated], if $\mathfrak m$ is not associated, it contains a nonzerodivisor on $M$, so $d\ge1$. Conversely, if $\mathfrak m$ is associated, every $x\in\mathfrak m$ kills the associated nonzero element, so there is no $M$-regular sequence of positive length in $\mathfrak m$; the empty sequence gives $d=0$. Consequently $d=0$ if and only if $\operatorname{Ext}^0_R(\kappa,M)
eq0$, proving the base case and giving, when $d>0$, both $\operatorname{Ext}^0_R(\kappa,M)=0$ and a nonzerodivisor $x\in\mathfrak m$ on $M$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00LW (lemma-depth-ext), proof paragraph beginning 'By Lemma lemma-ideal-nonzerodivisor'; Lemma Tag 00LL (lemma-ideal-nonzerodivisor), for I = m

proof.text: Suppose $d>0$. Since the finite supremum of regular-sequence lengths is $d$, a sequence $x,f_2,\ldots,f_d$ of length $d$ exists. Choose this $x$, which is a nonzerodivisor on $M$, and put $Q=M/xM$. The tail is $Q$-regular: the successive quotients $Q/(f_2,\ldots,f_j)Q$ equal $M/(x,f_2,\ldots,f_j)M$, and the last quotient is nonzero. Thus $Q$ is nonzero and finite, and its depth is at least $d-1$. Conversely every $Q$-regular sequence $g_1,\ldots,g_r$ in $\mathfrak m$ prepends with $x$ to an $M$-regular sequence: injectivity at the first position is the choice of $x$, and at all subsequent positions and for the last nonzero quotient the same quotient identification applies. Hence $r+1\le d$ for every such sequence, so $\operatorname{depth}(Q)=d-1$. The induction hypothesis gives $\operatorname{Ext}^j_R(\kappa,Q)=0$ for $j<d-1$ and $\operatorname{Ext}^{d-1}_R(\kappa,Q)\ne0$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00LW (lemma-depth-ext), choice of x with depth(M/xM) = depth(M)-1; the choice is justified directly from the maximal-length regular sequence and its quotient identifications, without invoking the later depth-drop lemma.

proof.text: Multiplication by $x$ is injective on $M$, so $0\to M\xrightarrow{x}M\to Q\to0$ is a short exact sequence. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ext-long-exact-second-variable] to it with first argument $\kappa$. Since $x\in\mathfrak m$, $x\kappa=0$, and [lem-weil-pbc-ext-annihilator-first-variable] says each map $\operatorname{Ext}^j_R(\kappa,M)\xrightarrow{x}\operatorname{Ext}^j_R(\kappa,M)$ in the long exact sequence is zero. Step 2 already gives $\operatorname{Ext}^0_R(\kappa,M)=0$ because $d>0$. For every $j\ge0$, exactness and the zero scalar maps give a short exact sequence $0\to\operatorname{Ext}^j_R(\kappa,M)\to\operatorname{Ext}^j_R(\kappa,Q)\to\operatorname{Ext}^{j+1}_R(\kappa,M)\to0$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00LW (lemma-depth-ext), displayed long exact Ext sequence and following sentence; Lemma Tag 00LU (lemma-long-exact-seq-ext); Lemma Tag 00LV (lemma-annihilate-ext)

proof.text: For $j<d-1$, the middle group $\operatorname{Ext}^j_R(\kappa,Q)$ in the short exact sequence of Step 4 is zero by Step 3, so both $\operatorname{Ext}^j_R(\kappa,M)$ and $\operatorname{Ext}^{j+1}_R(\kappa,M)$ are zero. Together with $\operatorname{Ext}^0_R(\kappa,M)=0$ from Step 2, this gives vanishing for all $j<d$. At $j=d-1$, the first group $\operatorname{Ext}^{d-1}_R(\kappa,M)$ is zero (from Step 2 when $d=1$, or from the preceding vanishing when $d>1$), while $\operatorname{Ext}^{d-1}_R(\kappa,Q)$ is nonzero by Step 3. The short exact sequence therefore identifies it with $\operatorname{Ext}^{d}_R(\kappa,M)$, which is nonzero. Thus $d$ is the least degree of nonzero Ext, completing the induction and giving existence of that degree.

mathlib_candidate.how: Rees' theorem (read by sed -n 130,175p): for R Noetherian, M finite with IM < M and n : ℕ, Ext^i(R/I, M) = 0 for all i < n iff there is an M-regular sequence of length n in I. With I = m this gives: depth(M) ≥ n iff Ext^i(κ,M) = 0 for i < n, once one adds (a) Nakayama (mM ≠ M for M nonzero finite over a local ring), (b) the agreement of Mathlib's RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular with the regular sequences of [def-weil-pbc-depth] and that a regular sequence of length ≥ n has an initial piece of length n which is regular, (c) Shrink (R ⧸ I) ≅ R/I and Mathlib's Ext against [def-pc-ext], and (d) finiteness of depth(M) (Stacks 00LR/00LK) for the existence of a nonzero Ext.
